_: Flesh, the floor of Biomes O' Plenty's Nether biomes, is its own family (Xep signed it off on 2026-11-07; W4 T17, carried from the 1.7.10 edition, which names BiomesOPlenty:flesh:0 from FTB Infinity's census). Read from Biomes O' Plenty 7.0.1's jar in the 1.12.2 Lawns copy: one state, sponge material, 0.4 to dig, the same short box as the 1.7.10 block, so the whole block is named.

From Enigmatica 2 Expert 1.93a's census of 1.12.2 (W4 R8, judged 2026-11-12). Dried sand is sand, where the rules read its ground material as dirt; the census judged the whole block, so it is named whole. The grass block's values 6 and 8 were seen only in Nether biomes, where they are the overgrown and mycelial netherrack tops, so nether, where the rules read the grass class; its other values stay the grass the rules give them, and the dirts, muds, sands and the other sandstones stay as the rules leave them.

White sandstone, value 0, the natural block, is solid natural rock as vanilla sandstone is, and the rules leave it out for its decorative word; named at that value alone, as 1.16.5's, 1.20.1's and the 26.x censuses ruled it, so the editions match (W4 R14, 2026-11-13). Its chiseled and smooth values, 1 and 2, are made, and its stairs and slabs are left to the rules.

A slab or stair takes its full block's ruling (Xep, 2026-11-13: Can we make it so all slabs of blocks that wear, also wear, in their own like the full blocks do? and: Same with stairs as slabs; W4 R15). These are this mod's slabs and stairs whose full blocks a census of 1.12.2 judged, each named at its full block's family so it wears on its own texture as the full block does, at the values that hold its full block's own material. A slab or stair of a block the census excluded, or never judged, is left as it was. Where an earlier note here leaves this mod's slabs and stairs to the rules, or to detection's family, the ones named below no longer are.
